Chapter 3
Nutrition Assessment: Foundation of the Nutrition Care Process  49
Body composition refers to distribution and size of all com-
ponents contributing to total body weight. In most clinical 
settings, body composition refers to two major components of 
total body weight: fat mass and fat-free mass. A more thorough
deﬁ nition would include fat mass, total body water, osseous
mineral (bone and teeth), and protein. Nutrition professionals
are most concerned about metabolically active tissue and ﬂ uid 
status. Techniques that allow assessment of these compart-
ments are necessary for the design of appropriate nutrition
interventions.
Measurement techniques such as skinfolds and bioelectrical 
impedance use portable equipment and can be easily ac-
complished in any setting. Other measurements using hy-
drodensitometry, air displacement plethysmography, or dual
energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) are used in outpatient
